2027-01-12.title: Second Tuesday of Denha
2027-01-12.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Abide in me; abide in my love
2027-01-12.verse: I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
theo: Yesterday Jesus prayed that we may be one; today the readings show what that unity looks like from the inside. Paul uses the image of the body: “For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ.” Notice that Paul does not end with the Church but with Christ himself: the Church is Christ's own Body, and we became its members in Baptism, for “in the one Spirit we were all baptized into one body”. No member may say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body.” The grandmother who prays her rosary quietly at the back, the catechism teacher, the young man who carries the processional cross: “God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.” Envy and self-contempt both forget this.

Jesus teaches the same truth with the image of the vine: “I am the vine, you are the branches.” Life flows from the vine into every branch; cut off, a branch withers. The Father is the vinegrower, and he prunes the fruitful branch “to make it bear more fruit”: our trials are often his pruning, not his rejection. Again and again in these verses Jesus says abide. It is the language of a home, of staying. “As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love.” We abide in him by keeping his word, by prayer, and above all in the Holy Qurbana, where he says to us once more: abide in me as I abide in you.
outline: Ask: what happens to a branch cut off from the plant?
Each of us belongs and is needed.
Staying with him through word, prayer and Qurbana.
“Apart from me you can do nothing.”
live: Thank one person in your parish whose service usually goes unnoticed.
Make one visit this week to Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament, simply to stay with him.
2027-01-12.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the vine and we are the branches. Keep me joined to you and to all the members of your Body. Prune in me whatever bears no fruit, and let me abide in your love, so that the Father may be glorified by the fruit of my life. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the many become one body, because all of us share the one Bread. Here the branches receive the life of the vine.

quick: We are one body in Christ, and every member is needed.
Jesus is the vine; apart from him we can do nothing.
We abide in his love by keeping his word.
2027-01-12.action: Thank one person whose service in the parish goes unnoticed.
2027-01-12.question: Am I staying close to the vine, or trying to bear fruit on my own?

family.explain: Jesus said he is like a vine and we are its branches. A branch stays green when it is joined to the vine. We stay alive in God when we stay close to Jesus.
family.intention: We pray that every member of our family may stay close to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we stay close to Jesus this week?”

illus: A pepper farmer in Wayanad showed a group of visiting students a vine climbing a silver oak. He cut one small branch and laid it on the ground. By evening its leaves had curled. He said: the branch did nothing wrong; it was only separated. That is what happens to us without Christ.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true vine, keep us joined to you and to one another as we gather. Amen.
share: The body does not consist of one member but of many (1 Corinthians 12:14). Do I value the gifts of others?
Apart from me you can do nothing (John 15:5). Where am I trying to manage without Jesus?
Abide in my love (John 15:9). What helps me to stay in his love?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your love.
interc: For the Church, the Body of Christ, that every member may be valued.
For those who feel useless or unwanted in the community.
For those cut off from the Church, that they may be joined to the vine again.
For those going through times of pruning and trial.
For our group, that we may bear much fruit.
pm.close: Father, vinegrower of our souls, keep us joined to your Son, prune us in love and let us bear fruit that lasts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul says that the Church is like a body: one body, many members. In the one Spirit we were all baptized into one body (1 Corinthians 12:13). The foot cannot say: I do not belong, because I am not a hand.

Some of us think we are too important; others think we are not important at all. Both forget that God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose (1 Corinthians 12:18). You are needed in the Body of Christ.

Jesus gives the same lesson with a vine: I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing (John 15:5). The secret of a fruitful life is not effort alone but staying joined to him.
Sometimes the Father prunes us. It hurts, but he does it so that we may bear more fruit. Let us abide in his love through his word, through our prayer and through the Holy Qurbana. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says he is a vine and you are a little branch. Stay close to Jesus every day with a prayer, and you will grow lovely fruit: kindness, joy and peace!

intro: Theme: “Apart from me you can do nothing.”
One body and one vine: our life is in Christ and in one another.

q: I praise you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Wonderful are your works; that I know very well.
For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ.
points.apply: Thank one person whose service in the parish goes unnoticed.

q: You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out the nations and planted it.
I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
points.apply: Begin each task this week with: Lord, apart from you I can do nothing.

q: the LORD appeared to him from far away. I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love.
points.apply: Visit Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament once this week.

concl: Each of us is a needed member of Christ's Body.
Joined to the vine, we bear much fruit.
2027-01-12.resolve: Stay with Jesus for five minutes each day this week, and thank one fellow member of the parish.
